title: late-arrival-converger-idempotent-patcher-with-linearizable-checkpointing
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Our usage analytics pipeline occasionally receives late-arriving or post-hoc event corrections (tombstones, patches, delayed enrichments). Current reprocessing tooling focuses on full replays and windowed backfills which are expensive and can create duplicate or conflicting aggregates when events mutate. This ticket proposes a new 'Late Arrival Converger' service: an idempotent, incremental patcher that applies differential event deltas to derived analytics tables with linearizable checkpointing to guarantee convergence and safe concurrent backfills.

Solution overview: Build a patch-oriented reconciliation runner that consumes a compact 'delta manifest' (list of event ids + change type) instead of replaying full streams. The runner will: 1) verify and apply per-partition patches with compare-and-swap (CAS) checkpoints; 2) be tombstone-aware to remove previously counted events; 3) support safety throttles and batch-size constraining policies to protect downstream OLAP stores; 4) emit deterministic progress markers for operator visibility and automated resume. The system will live as a Console backend service (k8s microservice) with a small reconciling worker pool and a coordinator that preserves linearizable checkpoints in DynamoDB (or equivalent) using conditional writes.

Why different from existing work: Instead of full-stream replays or naive idempotent re-ingest, this approach focuses on minimal-change delta application with explicit monotonic checkpoints to avoid wide-scale reprocessing, reduce credits usage for Hosted customers, and remove the 'replay storm' risk. It complements, but is not a replacement for, the historical backfill orchestrators.

Constraints and non-goals: Not intended to handle schema migrations (will leverage existing schema-migration flow). Not replacing heavy analytics recomputes when transformation logic changes; those remain full backfills. Not a low-latency hot path for user-facing queries; it's a batch/nearline reconciliation tool with SLOs around eventual consistency within configured windows.
notes: Prefer delta manifests generated by existing ingest layer (if available) to avoid scanning raw event store.
Checkpoint store design must support conditional compare-and-swap semantics; DynamoDB conditional writes chosen for prototype, evaluate Spanner/Cockroach alternatives later.
Need RBAC controls and audit logging for reprocess triggers (Console UI will call a private API endpoint).
Plan to reuse existing backpressure hooks from the bulk-backfill runner for OLAP safety throttling.
acceptance_criteria: Service can apply a manifest containing 100k small deltas and produce correct aggregates against a test OLAP cluster without duplicates.
Checkpoints are linearizable: concurrent patch runs for the same partition cannot cause lost updates; verified by deterministic unit + integration test.
Operator dashboard shows per-partition progress, current throughput, and per-batch failure reasons.
Automated resume works: interrupted run can resume from last committed checkpoint without re-applying completed batches.
End-to-end cost is at least 5x lower than an equivalent full-stream replay for typical correction workloads in benchmark tests.
implementation_steps: Design delta manifest schema and producer contract (event_id, partition_key, change_type, payload_hash, tombstone_flag, timestamp).
Prototype checkpoint table schema and CAS operations in DynamoDB with TTL for stale run cleanup.
Implement worker that consumes manifests from S3/GS or internal object store and performs patch apply with idempotent semantics.
Integrate OLAP safety throttle: max tokens per second, per-target-concurrency limits, and automatic slow-down when quota thresholds reached.
Add per-batch audit events to the telemetry pipeline for reconciliation event tracing.
Build Console endpoints and minimal UI for launching manifests, viewing progress, and aborting runs.
Create system/integration tests with seeded delayed events and tombstones to validate correctness under concurrency.
Staged rollout: internal canary -> broader infra team runbooks -> opt-in customer trials -> GA.
testing_plan: Unit tests for CAS checkpoint operations, including simulated conditional write failures and retries.
Integration tests with a local OLAP instance (Postgres/ClickHouse dev cluster) validating aggregate deltas.
Chaos test: kill worker mid-batch and assert resume from last checkpoint without double-apply.
Load test: submit synthetic manifests to validate throughput and safety throttling under stress.
Regression test: verify no regressions against existing backfill or replay tools by running both on same correction set on staging.
monitoring_and_alerting: SLOs: target run-success-rate >= 99% for manifests <= 500k deltas over 24 hours.
Alerts: high application error rate (>1% failed batches) -> oncall; stuck checkpoint progress for >30m -> operator pager.
Dashboards: per-partition latency histogram, batch success/failure counts, applied-delta QPS, and downstream OLAP lag.
Audit logs: every manifest launch/abort/operator action logged to secure audit sink for compliance.
comments: 2026-03-06 Maya Patel: Initial proposal drafted. Recommend focusing on manifest-first approach to limit IO and cost.
2026-03-07 Diego Alvarez: Assigned for prototype. Blocking question: do we force manifests from ingest or allow a scanner to emit deltas?
2026-03-08 Priya Nair (Data Eng): Prefer manifest generator in the ingest tier for accuracy; scanner fallback acceptable for legacy partitions.
2026-03-10 SRE Rotation-Bot: Note: ensure worker exposes /health and Prometheus metrics; bulk apply jobs must respect cluster node-class selectors.
